## Definition

An exact dyadic rational is a number $m2^q$ with integers $m,q$.
Fix integers $p\ge2$ and $e_{\min}\le e_{\max}$. Put
$\eta=2^{e_{\min}-p+1}$ and
$N_{\max}=(2^p-1)2^{e_{\max}-p+1}$. The finite representable set $\mathbb F$
consists of zero, both signs of every normal number $k2^{e-p+1}$ with
$e_{\min}\le e\le e_{\max}$ and $2^{p-1}\le k<2^p$, and both signs of every
subnormal number $k\eta$ with $1\le k<2^{p-1}$. The smallest positive
subnormal is $\eta$, the smallest positive normal is $2^{e_{\min}}$, and the
largest finite magnitude is $N_{\max}$. The extended endpoint set also contains
$-\infty$ and $+\infty$ as enclosure sentinels; they are not finite machine
numbers.

For a real $x$ with $|x|\le N_{\max}$, define $\operatorname{rd}(x)$ as the
greatest member of $\mathbb F$ not exceeding $x$, and $\operatorname{ru}(x)$ as
the least member of $\mathbb F$ not less than $x$. Define
$\rho(x)=\operatorname{ru}(x)-\operatorname{rd}(x)$. For nonzero $x$ in the
subnormal range, define the absolute-error bound $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)=\eta$;
for $2^e\le |x|<2^{e+1}$ in the normal range, define
$\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)=2^{e-p+2}$. At finite overflow, a directed result is
the corresponding infinite sentinel and its error bound is $+\infty$; the
status is `overflow`. The rounding procedure reports `finite`, `subnormal`, or
`overflow`, so no relative-error assumption is implicit.

An exact rational intermediate may be converted by comparing integer
numerators and denominators after clearing powers of two. A directed interval
endpoint is the resulting greatest lower or least upper member of $\mathbb F$.

## Statement

For finite $x$ with $|x|\le N_{\max}$, the directed roundings defined in
[[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]] satisfy
$\operatorname{rd}(x)\le x\le\operatorname{ru}(x)$ and each endpoint error is
at most the stated $\epsilon_{\rm abs}(x)$ (with zero error when $x$ is
representable). For $x>N_{\max}$ the pair $(N_{\max},+\infty)$ encloses $x$;
for $x<-N_{\max}$ the pair $(-\infty,-N_{\max})$ encloses $x$. Overflow has
error bound $+\infty$ and cannot be reported as a finite-error result.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite dyadic set $\mathbb F$, subnormal quantum $\eta$,
exponent limits, and endpoint roundings from
[[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]].

[L1] [[def-dyadic-floating-point-format-and-directed-rounding]]: adjacent
subnormals are spaced by $\eta$; in the normal bin
$[2^e,2^{e+1})$ the representable spacing is $2^{e-p+1}$; directed rounding
selects the adjacent representables bracketing the exact real number.

## Proof

1.1 If $x$ is representable, both directed roundings equal $x$. Otherwise there are consecutive representables $a<b$ with $a<x<b$: finiteness of $\mathbb F$ and the definitions of greatest lower and least upper values give these neighbors. Hence $\operatorname{rd}(x)=a\le x\le b=\operatorname{ru}(x)$. [given, L1, choose]

1.2 If $0\le x<2^{e_{\min}}$, both neighboring nonnegative representables are in the subnormal lattice with step $\eta$, so $x-a<\eta$ and $b-x<\eta$. If $2^e\le x<2^{e+1}$ is normal, consecutive representables within the bin are spaced by $2^{e-p+1}$. A bracket reaching the upper bin endpoint has no larger gap; in all cases each endpoint error is at most the stated, more conservative $2^{e-p+2}$. Symmetry of $\mathbb F$ gives the same bounds for negative $x$. [given, L1, algebra]

2.1 For $x>N_{\max}$, $N_{\max}<x<+infty$, and for $x<-N_{\max}$, $-\infty<x<-N_{\max}$; the prescribed extended endpoints therefore bracket $x$. The status and infinite absolute-error bound explicitly record that no finite error estimate is available outside the finite range. [given, algebra] ∎
